checkpoints.description: [1/2] Report the OS-assigned port when serve uses --port 0

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed port 0 binds to a real port (64944) while the CLI advertises http://127.0.0.1:0, which nobody can connect to.
impact_assessment.benefits: The startup message is always a usable URL, including for ephemeral-port runs.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: only the startup message changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive the URL from server_address after binding, add a failing-first test on a real bound server, and keep the fixed-port message unchanged.

checkpoints.head: 61f01b2e007ff25fa9d5ece9d5576243682dc008

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Refuse CLI writes while a serve process holds the single-writer lock

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed delete succeeds while the lock is held, so CLI writes can race server appends and atomic trims and lose data.
impact_assessment.benefits: The single-writer guarantee now covers every process that mutates the inbox.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: mutating CLI commands now fail while a server runs, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: none; concurrency: lock is acquired before any write and released in finally; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Acquire the same SingleWriterLock for clear/delete/import with a Why/Fix refusal, add failing-first tests for all three, and leave read commands unlocked.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Done: clear/delete/import refuse while the serve lock is held; reads still work; 85 tests green
[2/2] Done: README write rule and ADR-017
[2/2] Phase 4 passed: 5/5 gates green, 85 tests
Task 'postbox-writelock' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 76f13c756b0be88bee483d85fb3d8f78b277a5a0

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Return JSON 500 for undecodable inboxes and accept global flags after subcommands

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a non-UTF-8 byte drops the connection with a traceback instead of the documented JSON 500, and postbox list --json fails because global flags exist only before the subcommand.
impact_assessment.benefits: Corrupt files produce a consistent JSON error, and natural CLI flag placement works.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive flag placement, no change to existing forms; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add UnicodeDecodeError to the server error tuple, add suppressed-default copies of the global flags to every subparser, and add failing-first tests for both.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Done: undecodable inbox returns JSON 500; global flags accepted after subcommands; 88 tests green
[2/3] Done: README flag placement and non-UTF-8 note, ADR-018
[3/3] Phase 4 passed: 5/5 gates green, 88 tests

checkpoints.head: fa3100ee33baa54edaa4e1f3a8876d577e05c17b

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make lookup errors context-aware and machine-readable under --json

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed show/delete lookup failures print replay-specific guidance and emit human text under --json, breaking agent parsing.
impact_assessment.benefits: Each command explains its own failure, and agents get a parseable JSON error object.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: JSON error shape is new, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Parameterise the shared lookup helper with context and json_mode, reuse it in delete, and add failing-first tests for show/delete wording and JSON parsing.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Done: context-aware lookup errors, JSON error objects under --json, unified delete validation; 91 tests green
[2/2] Done: README agent-error format and ADR-019
